item.description: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. item.title: One Task, Many Interfaces: Simple Cross-Interface Consistency Training Improves LLM Agent Robustness
item.description: Post-training binds the competence of an LLM agent to the interface it was trained on. Semantics-preserving perturbations of that interface, such as renaming an action or changing the notation, leave the underlying task unchanged yet make the agent worse at it. item.title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
item.description: We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. item.title: Teaching Agents in their Own Style: Blackbox Teacher Distillation for Web Agents
item.description: Frontier web agents using closed models have high inference and computational costs. Smaller open models can be an alternative, but to be performant, they require training supervision from a human or teacher model. Token-level teacher distillation is not an option for closed teachers as it needs access to the model's logits. item.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
item.description: A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. item.title: Learning Individual Scientific Taste with Privileged Hindsight Distillation
item.description: Scientific taste shapes which research directions researchers pursue, and it varies across individuals. Existing work evaluates research directions along multiple evaluation criteria or models scientific taste using community feedback signals such as citations and reviews, but neither directly captures how individuals translate assessments under the same criteria into different preferences. item.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
item.description: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes. We call this property the recoverability of the teacher and show it fails on incorrect rollouts: the teacher follows student errors, although it recognizes them. item.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
item.description: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. item.title: Why 3D Reconstruction Breaks Down on Under-Ice AUV Video, and How to Predict It
item.description: Reconstruction of 3D structures using under-ice AUV video footage has been inaccurate, although it is not certain whether this is due to shortcomings in the methods or an inherent deficiency of the capture system. We test four different models for reconstruction on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video (Icefin, Kamb Ice Stream): classical feature matching SfM, differentiable photometric splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model. item.title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds
item.description: Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances. Existing evaluations of social agents mainly rely on LLM judges that rate the conversation, without checking the resulting plan. item.description: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. item.title: HM3D-M3: A Benchmark for Multi-Agent, Multi-Modal, Multi-Object Goal Navigation
item.description: Rapid progress in AI agents and robotics makes it a matter of the near future that humans are served by a team of robots. Such a team will receive several goals at once, each specified in whatever form is convenient for the human, such as a category name, a photo, or a spoken description. Existing benchmarks study multi-agent, multi-modal, and multi-object goal navigation in isolation, and a benchmark that places all three in one episode is missing. item.title: Accelerating VLA Inference with Perturbation Informed Execution
item.description: Action-chunking vision-language-action (VLA) models predict sequences of future robot actions. item.description: Long-horizon precise manipulation produces mixed-quality data for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models: even successful demonstrations and intervention-assisted rollouts may contain detours, hesitations, failed attempts, and imperfect recoveries. item.description: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. item.title: GAD: Geometry Attention Distillation for Consistent Video Generation
item.description: Video diffusion models generate visually compelling short-term sequences but often struggle to preserve scene geometry and object structure over time. In this paper, we first demonstrate that current video attention cannot identify reliable correspondences across frames, with responses dispersed across multiple regions even after recognizable scene structure has emerged. item.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
item.description: Reasoning models achieve strong performance through long chains of thought (CoT), but often spend more tokens than needed to solve a problem. Existing ways to shorten the CoT require additional training for each model, add a fixed steering vector to the model's hidden states, or use decoding heuristics such as stopping early or banning words like "wait", which can reduce accuracy. item.title: GUIDE: Computationally Augmented Consensus for Trustworthy Clinical Practice Guidelines
item.description: Maintaining up-to-date clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) is essential for evidence-based medicine, but rapid evidence growth and complex expert consensus formation limit timely updates. We developed GUIDE, a multi-agent copilot system for human-AI collaborative guideline generation and updating. GUIDE delegates labor-intensive tasks to specialized AI agents while preserving expert judgment and final arbitration. item.title: DuplexBridge: Coordinating Understanding and Generation for Unified Image Editing
item.description: Complex image editing requires faithful task interpretation and accurate execution, but a failed edit does not reveal which responsibility failed. We present DuplexBridge, which uses a unified model's own understanding capability to enhance prompts for its own generation capability, without an external understanding module. A source-grounded bridge specifies targets, final-state changes, and preservation constraints. item.description: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed? Offline imitation provides dense but token-specific supervision and can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. item.title: One Monitor Does Not Fit All: Formalism-Agnostic Runtime Verification for Agentic AI
item.description: Agentic AI systems combine model decisions, mutable state, tool calls, and delegation to external agents. Monitoring them requires observations from different execution boundaries, while prevention requires control before an operation produces its effect. We present AgenticRV, a runtime-verification architecture that separates these boundaries from the monitoring formalism. item.title: ReproBAIT: Can coding agents build their own biological AI tools?
item.description: Large language models are increasingly competent at leveraging scientific knowledge and existing computational tools to execute complex workflows. At present, little information exists on their ability to reconstruct tools when given limited descriptions of such tools. item.title: StateCraft: Augmenting Video World Models with Abstract-State Reasoning
item.description: Video world models aim to simulate complex environments with realistic appearance and dynamics. Maintaining consistency over long interactions requires tracking past actions and understanding how those actions affect the environment. Video world models can only generate partial observations of the entire world at a time. item.title: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models
item.description: Language captures only a subset of the perceptions, intuitions and intents that form meaning between speakers. What, then, are the limits of language? item.description: Speculative decoding's effectiveness is governed by two quantities: the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them. item.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. item.description: Long-output inference in large language models suffers from severe KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks. item.title: Text-Informed Training Data Filtering for Enhanced Virtual Flow Meter Performance
item.description: In sectors such as energy, aquaculture and chemical processing, the effectiveness of both mechanistic and data-driven models is frequently limited by poor-quality training data, which obscures underlying physical laws and degrades predictive accuracy. item.title: Energy Consumption Analysis of Discrete Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
item.description: As Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to scale, their energy consumption during inference has become a critical concern. item.title: ReGRA: Residual-Gradient Adaptation for Complementary Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
item.description: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning by learning low-rank weight updates. item.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
item.description: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. item.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
item.description: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). item.title: Unlocking Token Rewards via Training-Free Reward Attribution
item.description: In this paper, we propose an extremely efficient, training-free method to extract token-level reward signals directly from an existing deep reward model. This influence is defined as the change in the final macroscopic reward (e.g., the process reward) when a token is replaced with a semantically null token. item.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
item.description: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment.
